content.comment_body: I’ve never really considered how to properly manage version control until now. Should I look into using Github, or are there other solutions that work better? Up to now, I’ve just uploaded my files to OneDrive and saved several versions under different filenames. This led to a situation where I lost track of which version was deployed. To resolve it, I had to download the deployed program and compare it to my versions before I could add customer-requested features.

You don’t need development tools like Github for [product_name] projects, since you can write all your user programs for connected [product_name] devices into a single project file using the network mode in [product_name] software. I also use different filenames for different project versions. You can document version details within [product_name] software, or use a text or spreadsheet editor like MS Excel. If you’re working across various locations with different [product_name] devices, you can maintain a table noting each program and device version (including optional interface versions). This approach keeps things organized using basic tools. For additional safety, storing everything in two places, such as a secondary hard drive, acts as a backup.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working on [product_name] projects find manual versioning—via cloud storage and varied filenames—causes confusion over which version is actually deployed. Community advice highlights using built-in features in [product_name] software, such as network mode, comments, and external documentation (like Excel spreadsheets) to manually track software and device versions. However, the process relies heavily on manual methods, which increases the risk of errors since there’s no automatic way to manage version history or identify deployed versions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a simple, reliable system to monitor and organize multiple development versions, quickly identify the version deployed, and avoid the hassle of manual searching. Ideally, they’re looking for a solution that offers integrated version control or automatic history tracking.
